boundary.evidence: the gates read state through esk-paths and delegate grounding to task-receipt; no logic leak.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED overclaim: both asserted a forged operator waiver is 'made VISIBLE by the self-test and the log', but session-setup only checked the enforcement HOOKS (never read the waivers file) and no log existed, while session-setup even told the agent the exact waiver path - so a forged by:operator waiver was honored silently, defeating agent-cannot-self-waive while the docs claimed detection. The operator asked for honest framing on guarantees.
findings.resolution: fixed by IMPLEMENTING the claimed detection (the stronger option): session-setup now reads the operator waivers file and lists EVERY waiver in effect at session start, so a forged entry is surfaced; the comment and doc now name that exact mechanism. A discriminating session-setup test asserts an in-effect waiver is surfaced.

findings.where: esk-paths.resolvePath consumed by finish-check/edit-gate on a missing/unsafe session id
findings.finding: CONFIRMED fail-OPEN: with ESK_ENFORCE=1 and no explicit path, a missing/unsafe session_id made resolvePath return null, which both gates treated as 'not wired' -> a file-changing turn ended unchecked and edits proceeded ungated, while session-setup advertised 'the hooks still enforce using the base store' (false; sessionPaths throws on an unsafe id).
findings.resolution: fixed: when enforcementOn() and the path is unresolvable, finish-check BLOCKS (after the read-only check) and edit-gate DENIES (fail closed); session-setup's no-session-id message now says the gates fail closed. Discriminating tests pin both (exit 2 on a missing session id; read-only still exit 0).

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: both hand-rolled `enforcementOn() && isSafeSession(SESSION) ? sessionPaths(SESSION).X : null`, a second/third copy of the rule esk-paths.resolvePath centralizes.
findings.resolution: fixed: operatorWaivers uses resolvePath('waivers','ESK_WAIVERS_FILE',SESSION); checkReceipt keeps ESK_RECEIPT||rec.receiptPath then resolvePath for the derived leg; the now-unused isSafeSession/sessionPaths imports were dropped.

findings.finding: CONFIRMED: the self-test checked 4 of the 6 installed enforcement hooks, so a removed reload-skills was not warned at session start (esk-init --check still caught it).

CONFIRMED honest-scope gap: the canary exercises only allow/no-op paths, so a regression neutralizing block()/deny() would still pass it (it does correctly catch dead paths and does not depend on powershell).
findings.resolution: fixed: added an honest-scope comment stating it proves the wiring is live, not the block logic (which the scripts' own discriminating tests prove).

findings.finding: 'enforced at install time in PR-B' was inaccurate; waiver authority is enforced by the finish-check at runtime.
findings.resolution: fixed: reworded to name runtime enforcement + the session-setup surfacing.
